Subject: BetaCorp integration: SDK & auth questions / post-call recap

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the BetaCorp team. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can move the integration forward: 

1) Immediate next steps (action owners)
- BetaCorp: send current sample request/response for your chat flow (Alex)
- Redwood: share SDK quickstart & auth flow docs (Marissa) — attached the integration guide for reference.
- Tech sync: schedule 30m with your infra/ops + our infra eng (Neha) to confirm routing and private network setup.

2) Integration topics raised on the call (we want to make sure we answered each):
- SDK setup + auth: you mentioned SSO + service account calls. We support API keys and mTLS for Dedicated/Private. For hosted, tokens + optional IP allowlist. If you need token scoping, we can discuss short-lived tokens.
- Routing & fallbacks: we have policy-based routing for latency/cost tiers and auto-fallback to compatible model variants. Need to confirm which regions you plan to run from.
- Structured output/tool calling: Redwood supports structured JSON output via our chat API (tool-calling patterns and schema validation). We also expose a completions endpoint if you prefer simpler prompt/response semantics.
- Embeddings / reranker: we recommend embedding for retrieval + a small reranker model to improve precision. We can provide batch/streaming embedding endpoints and examples.

3) Request/response schema questions you asked (high-level answers, details below):
- Chat vs completions: chat is conversation-oriented with role/turn structure and better tool-calling primitives; completions accept a prompt and return a single or streaming generation. Token accounting differs slightly (chat includes role tokens).
- Tokenization & max_tokens: model-specific; we’ll provide your sample through our tokenizer to estimate token counts. We can enforce token limits and pad/trim logic on the SDK side.
- Stop sequences vs streaming semantics: streaming returns partial tokens as they generate; stop sequences are honored server-side and will terminate streaming when seen. We also support client-side stop handling if you prefer.

Questions for you (so we can prepare the tech sync):
- Can you share a redacted example of the chat payload and an example completion-style prompt for the same flow?
- Do you plan to use hosted Redwood or Dedicated/Private? (This determines auth and network options.)
- Any compliance constraints (SOC2, data residency) we should note before the sync?

I attached a short integration guide and will follow up with a proposed mutual action plan. If it helps, I can include some sample SDK snippets for both chat and completions in the tech sync.

Thanks,

--

Alex — thanks for the details and the sample. Confirming we can handle the Dedicated + mTLS + SCIM requirements; will have our security/compliance team reach out on specific evidence for EU residency.

Answering your numbered items quickly: 
1) Chat streaming + stop sequences: server-side stop detection is supported and will close the stream when the stop tokens are observed. However, because network conditions and client buffering can cause extra partial data to be delivered, we recommend client-side detection too (SDKs include helpers that optionally perform detection + preemptive close).

2) Structured tool calling: our chat SDK returns a typed ToolCall object in our official SDKs (Python/TS) when using the tool-calling schema. If you use a custom client, we provide OpenAPI specs and a JSON schema for tool outputs; parsing raw JSON is fine but the official SDKs will do the heavy lifting and validation for you.

3) Embeddings/reranker at scale: for ~100M docs we recommend an offline batched embedding pass (worker fleet) to seed vector DB and then incremental/streaming updates for deltas. Chunk size depends on your average doc length — 200-500 tokens per chunk is typical. Use locality-sensitive hashing (or vector index sharding) for initial prune then reranker model for top-K reordering. We'll share a recommended pipeline doc.

Alex / Marissa — quick technical notes I wanted to add ahead of the tech sync: 

- Tokenization & max_tokens: token counting is model-specific (we use byte-pair style tokenizers for most open models). For Dedicated we'll run your sample through the exact tokenizer for the model you pick and return a token estimate. Note: chat inputs include role metadata and sometimes JSON/metadata overhead — allow ~5-10% overhead for role tokens and structured fields.

- Streaming semantics: streaming sends chunks as they become available; server honors stop sequences and will terminate generation. The SDK exposes a streaming iterator and also an on_data callback. For strict termination (e.g., stop when '}}' seen), combine server-side stop plus client-side buffer scanning and cancel the stream if you see the delimiter to avoid processing partial trailing tokens.

- Stop vs max_tokens behavior: stop takes precedence when encountered; max_tokens is a hard cap (prevents runaway token usage). If you set both, expect the stream to end on whichever happens first. For safe shutdown in the SDK we recommend setting both a reasonable max and a stop pattern.

- Completions vs Chat: Chat supports structured messages and tool-calling semantics (we surface function/tool outputs as a typed object in the SDK). Completions are simpler and better for single-shot prompts. If you need structured JSON output reliably, use chat + tool-calling + schema validation. For very high-QPS low-latency single-turn queries, completions may be cheaper.

- Embeddings batching: for your scale, use offline batches of ~2048-8192 documents per worker depending on GPU memory, and write into an index with background re-sharding. Consider using approximate nearest neighbor index with a reranker as Marissa noted.

I'll bring a short checklist to the sync with code snippets (Python + Node) showing streaming + stop handling and a basic embedding batch runner.
